A level 1 one-shot adventure. Lord Percival Thistledown is throwing himself a grand celebration, and the villagers are paying for it. Literally. With winter approaching, the self-important lord has seized livestock, grain, supplies, and even farm carts to fund a week of extravagant festivities. Meanwhile, his subjects are struggling to put food on their tables. But the villagers of Briarwood have had enough. With a little courage, a questionable plan, and the help of a passing adventurer, they might just pull off the most audacious feast in the lord's history. A lighthearted fantasy heist featuring colorful villagers, ridiculous nobility, questionable disguises, and a chance to give an entire village something worth celebrating.

Lionel pulls ahead of you at the last moment, crossing the finish line first, but just barely.
The crowd along the hedges is mostly silent, but one or two applaud his win as Barnaby and Tobias slow to a stop, panting as they sit down right where they are.

There are three more carts lined up alongside yours and the other three riders call out introductions.
Amos lifts a lace handkerchief high in the air. He lets it drop, signaling the start of the race. Barnaby and Tobias lean in and the cart lurches forward.
You and the other riders fall silent as a man steps up onto the stand, scroll in hand. The ring of keys at his belt jingles every time he moves.
The celebration continues for the rest of the week. From the village, you can hear music and laughter drifting down from the manor every night.
The crowd along the hedges cheers as Barnaby and Tobias slow to a stop, panting as they sit down right where they are.
You pull ahead of Lionel at the last moment, crossing the finish line first, but just barely.
Lord Percival looks at you, then at the two men who pulled your "chariot" and decides to be gracious.

You don't see anything by the pond edge so you lean over the sluice for a better look. The bank gives way under you and you slide down into the water up to your waist. Shivering, you climb out to see the glint of something shiny on your sleeve. Brushing the rest of the mud off, you see it's a copper ring.
Work out where she'd most likely have dropped it.
Search the mud along the pond edge.

You remember the notice about Nell's ring and walk over to the edge of the millpond. The ground near the sluice gate is now trampled mud from the milling crowd.

You bring the empty platter back to the kitchen and ask Hester about other ways into the storehouse. She tells you about a service hatch with a broken lock. Nobody ever bothered with it since the hatch has been stuck for years.

You muffle the keys in your apron and head back to the kitchen. Hester holds onto the keys for you until you're ready for the next phase of the plan.
You bring the next platter out to the great hall just in time.
You carry platters back and forth from the kitchen. Hester was right, nobody even looks at you.

Lift the keys while he's whispering.
